caveat.description: What can mislead about this artifact.

produced_by.description: endpoint id | receipt id | client_js | browser | user_action | service_wallet
produced_by.title: Produced By

receipt_ref.description: Receipt whose content templates parse this artifact.
receipt_ref.title: Receipt Ref

Attr.description: Provenance block carried by every fact and every record.
Attr.title: Attr

Cell.description:
One cell of the fact-by-source matrix. In YAML a cell is written as a string:
`recovered`, or `recovered: letter body` (value, colon, free-text detail).
Cell.title: Cell

CellValue.description: Table 3 vocabulary: what a source yields for a fact.
CellValue.title: CellValue

name.description: Cookie NAME only, never a value.
name.title: Name

field_facts.description: Request field name -> canonical fact it carries.
field_facts.title: Field Facts

gate.description: Mechanisms required; an empty list means open.

lookup_key.description: Fact the endpoint looks an order up by.

Fact.description: Canonical transaction facts: the comparison axis across services.
Fact.title: Fact

GateMechanism.description: An endpoint's gate is a list of these (empty list = open).
GateMechanism.title: GateMechanism

justification.description: Why this is service-level, not instance data.
justification.title: Justification

MatrixSource.description: Columns of the fact-by-source matrix, in display order.
MatrixSource.title: MatrixSource

facts.description: The facts this finding explains; empty means every fact absent from the location's column.
facts.title: Facts

implication.description: What the absence means for an examiner.

case_ref.description: Pointer to the case file / evidence log, never its contents.
case_ref.title: Case Ref

conditions.description: Acquisition conditions of a disk image: how the browser and the machine were closed, what else the profile holds.
conditions.title: Conditions

os.description: Operating system of the subject machine, e.g. Windows 10
os.title: Os

describes.description: The fact this pattern matches, if any.

field_map.description: Printed label -> fact it introduces in the receipt text.

boundary_markers.description: Lines that open / close a signed block.
boundary_markers.title: Boundary Markers

ReplayResult.description: One variant of the four-request replay protocol and what its reply showed.
ReplayResult.title: ReplayResult

validity_default.description: Applies to every attribute without its own validity.

literals.description: Service-level literals that occur verbatim in the text (e.g. a signing address).
literals.title: Literals

text.description: Literal response / document text with <placeholders> for instance values.
text.title: Text

yields.description: Facts carried by the fact-bearing placeholders, in order.
yields.title: Yields

Tier.description:
Stage of the transaction at which a fact can first be established. The observation
kind (capture, disk image, operator page, replay, explorer) records HOW it was seen.
Tier.title: Tier

Validity.description: When a value was true. Front ends change: a superseded record is kept and dated.

superseded_by.description: Path of the record that replaces this one.
superseded_by.title: Superseded By

Validity.title: Validity

description: One mixer service's invariant record (codes defined in knowledge_base/definitions.yaml). Every fact is an Attribute (value, tier 0 = no funds / 1 = funded, confidence observed|inferred|claimed|unknown, sources = observation ids). Instance data (specific addresses, TXIDs, order IDs, cookie values, amounts, timestamps) is rejected by the Python validators and belongs in a per-case findings file, never the KB.
title: mixerscope ServiceEntry v0.4
